title: Model Compare: current screen and real mask agreement
description: Find the nested comparison screen, load real fields, and use the working compare_masks API on genuine saved segmentations. Understand agreement without claiming ground truth, competing model weights or repaired GUI inference.
objectives: Find Model Compare inside Make Masks and load the actual example fields.
Recognize the current Cellpose incompatibility and separate it from the working pure-mask API.
Interpret object counts, matching, overlap and foreground disagreement without calling either result correct.
prerequisite: Recorded on spaCR 1.5.0.7 nightly with Cellpose 4.2.1.1. The current GUI comparison backend sends the unsupported invert argument. We load fields but do not start GUI inference, inject results or patch application code. The successful example calls spacr.model_compare.compare_masks on two actual saved outputs from Apply Cellpose's cell_pair_02.tif: stock cpsam batch preprocessing versus stock cpsam live-preview preprocessing. These use the SAME model weights, not two competing models. Both were independently checked in the Apply recording, but neither is expert ground truth. No model runs in this example. Preserve field identity, pixel geometry, preprocessing and file hashes; a matching shape alone does not establish that two masks describe the same image. The recorded helper and source hashes are in tools/tutorials/model_compare_example.py and its evidence receipt. Example output folders must be new. The agreement measures do not establish accuracy, model ranking, biological validity or out-of-sample performance.

scenes.narration: Model Compare is nested inside Make Masks. It is designed to compare segmentation results on the same fields. This lesson shows the current screen, then demonstrates its working mask-comparison API with two genuine saved outputs.

The screen separates Model A and Model B settings. Record the exact weights and preprocessing for each comparison. Different names or a larger object count do not establish that one result is better. The parameter and result tables are empty before a comparison runs.

Enter the real example folder and press Load. Here, three original fields load successfully and Compare becomes available. Loading images is not the same as successfully running the models. We have not created masks or filled the comparison table on this screen.

The installed Cellpose version rejects an invert argument still passed by this GUI backend. This real signature check shows the incompatibility without starting inference. We do not hide it. Instead, the next example uses compare_masks directly on existing label images.

Both masks belong to the same real image from the Apply Cellpose tutorial. One is its saved batch output; the other is its saved live-preview output. They use the same model with different preprocessing, not two competing sets of weights. Neither mask is ground truth.

The API reports ninety-four objects in A and ninety-five in B, with ninety-one matched pairs. Mean overlap among matched pairs is about zero point nine six. The adjusted Rand index is also about zero point nine six one. These describe agreement, not accuracy or a winner.

Inspect the actual saved overlays. The right panel marks pixels whose foreground status differs. It does not show every instance-label disagreement. A similar object count can conceal different boundaries, splits or merges, so inspect images as well as summary numbers.

The helper independently checks every matched overlap using the original pixels and verifies the identical-mask control. Keep the CSV, figure, source identities and preprocessing records together. Use independent reviewed annotations and held-out images before making accuracy or model-selection claims.
